name: Baton 4
shortDescription: A pocket light that actually gets carried.
description: 1300 lumens from something the size of a car key fob. Magnetic charging means no cables to lose, and the clip disappears in a pocket the way a good EDC light should.
why: Most EDC lights get left in a drawer after week one. This one doesn't, because it solves the two things people actually complain about: charging friction and pocket bulk.

name: Bugout
description: S30V blade, grivory handles, and a weight so low you'll forget it's clipped in until you need it. Built for people who carry a knife every day, not just on weekends.
why: It disappears until the moment you need it, then it's exactly sharp enough. That's the whole job of an EDC knife, done without extra weight or ceremony.

name: ProTac 2L-X
shortDescription: The light that shows up in every range bag.
description: Dual-fuel, 500 lumens, and a strobe mode that isn't a gimmick. Runs on CR123A or AA, so you're never stuck without a battery that fits.
why: It's the light we've seen carried by more range regulars than anything else, and there's a reason — it just works, every time, without babysitting.

name: Everyday Sling 6L
description: Weatherproof shell, a main compartment that opens flat, and organization that doesn't require you to think about it. Small enough for a quick errand, structured enough for a full day out.
why: A sling only earns a spot in rotation if it's fast to access and doesn't look like a camera bag. This one clears both bars.

name: Small Sebenza 31
shortDescription: The knife other knives get compared to.
description: Machined from titanium and CPM Magnacut, assembled by hand in the US. The tolerances are tight enough that you notice the difference the first time you flick it open.
why: It's expensive because the fit and finish justify it, not because of the name on the blade. Once you've handled one, cheaper folders feel loose by comparison.

name: Wave Plus
shortDescription: Seventeen tools, one thing that actually matters: it's always in the bag.
description: Pliers that don't flex, replaceable wire cutters, and a blade you can open one-handed. The multi-tool that ends up in the glovebox, the junk drawer, and the backpack, all at once.
why: There's a reason this shape hasn't changed much in twenty years. It's the rare tool that's genuinely useful instead of just full of gadgets.

name: PMAG 30 GEN M3
shortDescription: The standard everyone else gets measured against.
description: Impact-resistant polymer, an anti-tilt follower, and a price that means you can actually own enough of them. Not exciting. Just correct.
why: Boring is a compliment here. It runs without drama, which is exactly what you want at the range and nowhere else.

name: GR1
shortDescription: Built to outlast the rest of what you own.
description: 1000D Cordura, a laptop compartment that actually protects a laptop, and stitching that's overbuilt on purpose. It costs more up front and less over a decade.
why: We've seen these age into softer, better versions of themselves after years of daily use. That's not a common trait in bags at any price.

name: Paramilitary 2
shortDescription: The knife people recommend when asked for just one.
description: A compression lock that doesn't loosen over time, a blade shape that handles everything from mail to whittling, and a clip position that actually rides right.
why: It shows up on almost every serious EDC list for a reason — it does nothing flashy and everything well.

name: TINI 2
shortDescription: Smaller than your keys, brighter than you'd expect.
description: 500 lumens from a light that weighs less than an ounce. Ships with a real keyring, not an afterthought, and charges over USB-C in about an hour.
why: It's the light we hand to people who say they'd never carry one. Small enough that carrying it stops being a decision.

name: 6390RDS ALS
shortDescription: Retention that doesn't fight you when it matters.
description: The ALS lever releases with a natural draw motion, not a separate step you have to think about. Built for red-dot equipped pistols without needing a separate cut.
why: Retention holsters are a compromise by nature. This is the version of that compromise that trains the fastest and fails the least.

name: Cadet Alox
shortDescription: Proof that useful doesn't need to be complicated.
description: A blade, a nail file, scissors, and a screwdriver tip, all in an aluminum handle that gets better looking with wear. No gimmicks, no bulk.
why: This is the tool people carry for thirty years and then buy their kids the same one. That's the whole review.
